description: Fixes for workplace bottlenecks found in calendar, time, project-tool and CRM data (scenario A). Effect sizes and cost models are calibrated so the engine reproduces the two reference reports: Veloran (v1.0, Nov 1 2026) and Corlander & Vale (v1.0, Nov 4 2026). Vendors are examples to test in demos, not endorsements; prices are indicative until quoted.

status_duplication.label: Status reporting repeated across tools and meetings

review_queue.label: Work waiting in review, with rework

manual_keying.label: Source documents keyed in by hand

ai_capacity_forecasting.name: AI forecasting agent
ai_capacity_forecasting.how_it_solves: An agent in the firm's own CRM predicts roll-offs and demand from pipeline and booking history, then proposes staffing moves for a person to approve
example_vendors: Agentforce in the firm's own Salesforce org

effort.note: High: needs 12+ months of clean staffing data

governance.note: Medium: reads pipeline and staff data; every move needs human sign-off
governance.data_accessed: Pipeline, bookings and skills (internal; personnel data)
go_live_gates: Approve a one-page AI acceptable-use policy
A named person signs off every staffing move the agent proposes

requires.why: an AI forecast needs at least 12 months of clean booking data
requires.revisit: once the PSA holds 12 months of bookings

risks: Forecasts are only as good as the staffing history behind them
ai_capacity_forecasting.evidence: Veloran reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 1, Option 1

psa_tool.name: PSA tool
psa_tool.how_it_solves: One system holds bookings, roll-offs, skills and pipeline demand on a single timeline, eight weeks out

effort.note: Medium: data migration and new habits for {employees_total} people

risks: Must sync with the CRM and replace the current time tool
psa_tool.evidence: Veloran reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 1, Option 2

capacity_council.name: Capacity council and bench-to-certification
capacity_council.how_it_solves: A 30-minute weekly meeting books the next eight weeks; any unbooked day defaults to a certification plan or a reusable asset

effort.note: Low: one meeting and one rule

risks: Discipline; savings stall if leaders skip the meeting
capacity_council.evidence: Veloran reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 1, Option 3

ai_meeting_notes.name: AI meeting notes and status drafts
ai_meeting_notes.how_it_solves: AI joins calls, writes notes and drafts weekly status from transcripts and the work tracker

governance.note: High: records client calls that carry client data; some states require every party's consent to record
governance.data_accessed: Call audio and transcripts, including client data
go_live_gates: Consent from every party before any call is recorded
Approve a one-page AI acceptable-use policy
Vendor review: no training on client data

requires.why: recording client calls needs every party's consent and an approved AI policy first

conflicts_with.why: it would summarize meetings the reset cancels

ai_meeting_notes.evidence: Veloran reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 2, Option 1

system_of_record.name: One system of record
system_of_record.how_it_solves: All delivery work moves into the one tracker the firm already licenses; client reports generate from it; the duplicate tools retire
example_vendors: {work_tracker} dashboards and a client report template ({work_tracker} is already licensed)
example_vendors_fallback: Dashboards in the tracker already licensed, plus a client report template

effort.note_fallback: Medium: every active project must be migrated

requires.why: it assumes a work tracker is already licensed

risks: Clients used to other report formats need a new one
system_of_record.evidence: Veloran reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 2, Option 2

meeting_reset.name: Meeting and status reset
meeting_reset.how_it_solves: Recurring internal status meetings end; a five-line written update per project every Friday and one 30-minute weekly risk review replace them
risks: Meetings creep back without a named owner
meeting_reset.evidence: Veloran reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 2, Option 3

ai_timesheets.name: AI-drafted timesheets
ai_timesheets.how_it_solves: An app drafts each person's day from calendar, tracker and document activity; the person edits and submits. Drafts are visible only to the employee.

effort.note: Low: install plus a privacy briefing

governance.note: Medium: reads calendar and app activity. Mitigated by on-device processing, employee-only drafts and no manager access to raw activity
governance.data_accessed: Calendar titles, tracker activity, app and document names on the employee's laptop
go_live_gates: Approve a one-page AI acceptable-use policy
Security and contract review of the timesheet tool, including no-training terms
Drafts stay employee-only; managers never see raw activity

risks: Must export to the PSA if one is chosen
ai_timesheets.evidence: Veloran reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 3, Option 1

psa_time_module.name: PSA time module
psa_time_module.how_it_solves: Time entry moves into the PSA chosen for staffing, next to bookings, with approvals in one place
example_vendors: Same vendor as the PSA tool
psa_time_module.cost_note: $0 extra once the PSA tool is approved

implementation.label: Arrives with the PSA, weeks 6 to 8

risks: Moves the same manual entry to a new screen
psa_time_module.evidence: Veloran reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 3, Option 2

daily_time_rule.name: Daily time rule
daily_time_rule.how_it_solves: Log time before leaving each day: a 4:30 p.m. chat nudge, a 15-minute end-of-day calendar block, and on-time rates shared by team, never by name
risks: The habit fades without the nudge and team-level feedback
daily_time_rule.evidence: Veloran reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 3, Option 3

ai_followup_assistant.name: AI follow-up assistant
ai_followup_assistant.how_it_solves: AI inside the email client drafts follow-up emails from each client thread and summarizes long threads; staff still send and track them
example_vendors: Microsoft 365 Copilot Business (if the firm runs Microsoft 365)

governance.note: Medium: reads client email that holds confidential data; needs the AI policy and consent language first
go_live_gates: Approve a one-page AI acceptable-use policy
Client consent language for AI processing

risks: Drafts better emails but keeps no list, so nothing is tracked
ai_followup_assistant.evidence: Corlander & Vale reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 1, Option 1

client_portal.name: Client portal with automatic reminders
client_portal.how_it_solves: Every request becomes a tracked list in a portal; clients upload against each item; reminders go out automatically until the list is complete

effort.note: Medium: {portal_seats} staff and their clients learn a new portal
effort.note_fallback: Medium: staff and clients learn a new portal

risks: Often the largest licence cost in the program
client_portal.evidence: Corlander & Vale reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 1, Option 2

intake_desk.name: Intake desk and document deadline
intake_desk.how_it_solves: One intake desk sends one combined request list per client, logs receipts and chases on a fixed schedule; anything incomplete on the deadline is extended by rule

upfront.item: Request-list templates, engagement-letter wording and desk training

effort.note: Medium: clients must hear the deadline in their engagement letters, and partners must hold it

intake_desk.evidence: Corlander & Vale reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 1, Option 3

ai_pre_review.name: AI pre-review agent
ai_pre_review.how_it_solves: An agent reconciles each prepared return with its source documents and the prior year, and flags differences and risky items before a person reviews

effort.note: Medium: integration and client consent work

governance.note: High: full returns and source documents go to a third-party AI; needs signed client consent and a vendor review
go_live_gates: Signed client consent for AI processing
Approve a one-page AI acceptable-use policy

requires.why: full client files would go to a third-party AI, which needs signed client consent and a vendor review first
an AI pre-review works best on work that arrives complete through a tracked queue
requires.revisit: after one season on the portal

risks: The vendor may not support the firm's software version
A clean AI check can breed false comfort
ai_pre_review.evidence: Corlander & Vale reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 2, Option 1

review_queues.name: Review queues in the portal
review_queues.how_it_solves: Every item carries a status, a named reviewer and a due date; reviewers see their queue and its age; review notes are logged per item
example_vendors: Same vendor as the client portal
review_queues.cost_note: $0 extra once the client portal is approved
risks: Depends on the client portal decision
review_queues.evidence: Corlander & Vale reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 2, Option 2

tiered_review.name: Tiered review and review-ready checklist
tiered_review.how_it_solves: Preparers clear a one-page checklist before review; work is tiered by complexity so trained seniors sign off the simplest third and partners review only the complex third; a monthly debrief fixes the most repeated notes

effort.note: Medium: senior reviewers must let go of simple work

risks: Quality must hold under peer review
tiered_review.evidence: Corlander & Vale reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 2, Option 3

ai_document_extraction.name: AI document extraction
ai_document_extraction.how_it_solves: Software reads scanned documents, bookmarks them, extracts the data and fills the return; the preparer checks flagged fields instead of typing

upfront.item: Set-up, scanning standards and a pilot

effort.note: Medium: new scanning habits and a verification step

governance.note: Medium: documents are processed by a vendor; confirm US-only processing, no training on client data and deletion terms
governance.data_accessed: Scanned client documents and return data
go_live_gates: Vendor security and contract review: US-only processing, no training on client data, deletion terms
Client consent for AI processing in engagement letters

ai_document_extraction.evidence: Corlander & Vale reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 3, Option 1

import_first.name: Import-first standard and training
import_first.how_it_solves: Everything that can be imported is imported; staff get short training and a one-page import checklist
example_vendors: Import features already licensed in the firm's software
risks: The habit fades without spot checks
import_first.evidence: Corlander & Vale reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 3, Option 2

offshore_data_entry.name: Offshore data-entry partner
offshore_data_entry.how_it_solves: Scanned documents go to an outsourced team that keys them overnight; staff check the result

effort.note: High: signed consent from every client in scope; quality control across time zones

governance.note: High: sending client data outside the US needs each client's signed consent
go_live_gates: Signed consent from every client in scope

requires.why: sending client information outside the US needs every client's signed consent first

offshore_data_entry.evidence: Corlander & Vale reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 3, Option 3

pair_overlaps.together_note: The PSA makes capacity visible, the council turns it into decisions, and the certification rule gives every unplanned free day a use.

pair_overlaps.overlap_note: Both forecast capacity; the PSA's booking data is what the agent later learns from.

pair_overlaps.together_note: The reset frees most of the time at once, and one system of record stops the copying behind the remaining updates.
The rule fixes when time is logged; the drafts fix the effort and the forgetting.

pair_overlaps.overlap_note: Once the PSA is live, drafts flow into it instead of the old time tool; no extra savings are counted, to avoid double counting.

pair_overlaps.together_note: The intake desk owns the chase, and the portal does the remembering.

pair_overlaps.overlap_note: The intake desk takes over most of the chasing the assistant would help with.
The portal sends reminders without anyone writing them.

pair_overlaps.together_note: The checklist cuts second reviews at the source, tiering moves simple work off senior desks, and the queue shows everyone what is waiting.
Extraction removes most typing on complex documents; the standard stops anyone typing what already exists as data.
